solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scrounger's location beyond usual area

indicators.note: beyond says the location comes after the usual area in the answer

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level, as in 'feeling below par'
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A sponger has wandered somewhere outside their usual stamping ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usual' reads as part of the phrase 'usual area', but it is par, as in 'up to par'. 'beyond' places the location last.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is someone who lives off others without giving anything back, exactly a scrounger.

clue.text: European's quiet word of approval

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
ole is the Spanish cry of approval heard at bullfights

explanation.surface: A continental visitor murmurs a soft word of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole comes from Poland, a country of Europe.

clue.text: Phoned and spoke

definitions.meaning: the past participle of ring, to telephone
a crosspiece, such as the spoke of a chair or a ladder step

explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' reads as the past of speak; it is the noun for a bar or rung.
explanation.definitionFit: Having rung someone means having called them; a spoke or rung is a crossbar between uprights.

clue.text: Railway engineer sent phones for repair

indicators.note: sent for repair means the letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer on the railway has had his telephones sent off to be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive and is known as the father of the railways.

clue.text: Back street containing inferior soldiers

indicators.note: back means the whole construction is read in reverse
containing means the street abbreviation holds the next word inside it

parts.note: poor means inferior in quality

explanation.surface: Low-grade soldiers are stationed in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' makes SPOORT; 'Back' turns it round. 'Back street' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers, especially in numbers.

clue.text: Notice difficulty

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to notice it
a ... of bother is a difficulty, as in 'in a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Spot as a verb means catch sight of; as a noun, a tight spot is a predicament or trouble.

clue.text: Royal person in car initially surrounded by media

indicators.note: surrounded by means the media word goes round the other letters

parts.note: the press is the news media

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A royal in a car is mobbed by journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives C, and 'surrounded by' puts INC inside PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family.

clue.text: Briefly handle certain wealth stored up

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to treat something is to handle or deal with it
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An instruction to deal quickly with a definite stash of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of riches accumulated and kept, often hidden away.

clue.text: Legendary knight's weapon, an item for auction

parts.note: a lance is a long jousting weapon
a lot is a single item put up for sale at an auction

explanation.surface: A sale-room catalogue lists a famous knight's weapon among the items going under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot is the Round Table knight of Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Police force heading west, and east, take great risks

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: Detectives heading off in both directions are chancing their luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice, as in 'dice with death', is to gamble recklessly with danger.

clue.text: Fast celebrity on holiday, missing California

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the celebrity above the holiday word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: missing means the state abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: vacation is the American word for holiday
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A famous person on a break, away from California, is going without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes CA out of VACATION to leave VATION. 'Fast' reads as an adjective; it is the noun for going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast is a period of going without food, and starvation is the extreme of that deprivation.

clue.text: Oriental cutlery stays on cut of meat

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'stays on cut of meat' places the staying word after the cut

parts.note: a chop is a cut of pork or lamb
sticks means stays put or remains

explanation.surface: An instruction that Eastern eating utensils remain resting on a piece of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks are the pair of slim sticks used for eating in East Asia, so they serve as its cutlery.

clue.text: Woman, with time in prison, spotted beetle

parts.note: a lady is a woman
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: A woman who has served a prison term is seen with a spotted beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is the British name for the red, black-spotted beetle Americans call a ladybug.

clue.text: The Italian reclines in street — most stupid

indicators.note: in means the preceding words go inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: il is the Italian for 'the'
lies means reclines

explanation.surface: An Italian man stretched out in the road is behaving very foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Silliest is the superlative of silly, meaning foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Relocated in same French city

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has moved house but stayed within the same French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in northern France, capital of Picardy.

clue.text: Rubber tyres a repairman partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic only half-heartedly turns down some car tyres he was offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds RESARE in the clue words and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the thing used to rub out pencil marks.

clue.text: A pair of females ventilate business

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF
to air a room is to ventilate it

explanation.surface: Two women open the windows of a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Colour of banana, next to sink, is a warning sign

indicators.note: next to puts the two pieces side by side, colour first

parts.note: a ripe banana is yellow
to flag is to tire or sink in energy

explanation.surface: A banana-coloured mark beside the kitchen sink serves as a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow flag is waved, for example in motor racing, to warn of danger ahead.

clue.text: Type of brandy Republican kept in raincoat

indicators.note: kept in means the abbreviation is held inside the raincoat word

parts.note: mac, short for mackintosh, is a British word for a raincoat

explanation.surface: A Republican politician has stashed a bottle of brandy in his coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed for wine.

clue.text: List of dishes chaps start to upgrade

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: start to means take only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Some blokes set about improving a restaurant's bill of fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the card listing a restaurant's available food.

clue.text: Couple one encountered upon return

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upon return says the word for encountered comes back the other way

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Two people met each other again when one came back from a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantically linked pair are informally called an item.

clue.text: Friend with ideas altered fence of stakes

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mate with new plans has changed a stake fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a defensive barrier made of pointed wooden stakes.

clue.text: Attorney outside of the court

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor

indicators.note: outside of means taking just the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A lawyer is waiting outside the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' takes TE from 'the'. 'Court' looks like a law court; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, and to date is to go out with them romantically.

clue.text: Magnificent rowing team picked up famous wine

parts.note: grand means magnificent or splendid

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: the crew of a boat is its rowing team

explanation.surface: A splendid rowing eight celebrated with a renowned vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' gives CRU, the French spelling that sounds like CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand cru is the top classification of French vineyards, so the label marks a celebrated vintage.
